summary: Requested the heartbeat account's last field-relevance test: replace the synthetic sleep in the term-write race with a real file write plus fsync on every current-term update. The follower race, request shapes and 200-attempt count are unchanged; only the source of the write latency differs, and the result event now reports the measured mean and maximum latency so the receipt shows what was exercised. A local probe produced 73 inversions out of 200 with a mean term write of about 2.4 ms and a maximum of about 6.6 ms, which is the order of ordinary containerised fsync latency and would show the exposure under storage behaviour a deployment actually has rather than an injected delay. The earlier jitter receipts remain the low-latency control, so the experiment carries a single case and one comparison asserting that no attempt ends below the higher term it was sent. The submission validates with zero schema errors, the harness file exists, and it requests one execution.
